plants.name: Lavandula angustifolia
plants.description: An aromatic evergreen shrub with silvery-gray foliage and slender spikes of fragrant flowers that attract bees and butterflies. It thrives in full sun and well-drained soil and is widely grown in gardens and commercial fields.
plants.bloomingSeason: Early to late summer (June to August in the Northern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Mediterranean region; widely cultivated in Provence (France), England, Tasmania, and the northern United States
plants.funFact: Lavender has been used for over 2,500 years, and the name comes from the Latin 'lavare', meaning 'to wash', since the Romans scented their baths with it.

plants.name: Helianthus annuus
plants.description: A tall annual with a large, coarse stem and a showy flower head made of ray florets surrounding a disc of tiny fertile florets. Young flower heads track the sun across the sky.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid-summer to early fall (July to September in the Northern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Native to North America; cultivated across Europe, Russia, Ukraine, and Argentina
plants.funFact: A sunflower head is not a single flower but a composite of up to 2,000 tiny florets, arranged in spirals that follow the Fibonacci sequence.

plants.name: Nelumbo nucifera
plants.description: An aquatic perennial that rises from muddy water with large, round, water-repellent leaves and spectacular fragrant blooms held above the surface. Seed pods that follow the flowers resemble shower heads.
plants.bloomingSeason: Summer (June to September in the Northern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Asia and northern Australia; cultivated in ponds and lakes worldwide, notably in India, China, Vietnam, and Japan
plants.funFact: Lotus leaves have a micro-structured surface that causes water and dirt to roll off, a phenomenon known as the 'lotus effect' that has inspired self-cleaning materials.

plants.name: Epilobium angustifolium
plants.description: A tall perennial wildflower that forms dense stands with long spikes of bright magenta flowers that open from the bottom upward. It is often one of the first plants to colonize burned or cleared land.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid to late summer (July to September)
plants.location: Northern temperate and subarctic regions, including Alaska, Canada, the Pacific Northwest, Scandinavia, and Siberia
plants.funFact: Locals in northern regions say that when fireweed blooms reach the top of the spike, summer is nearly over.
